description: Test prompts and objective assertions for the paper-digest skill. Assertions map to checks in scripts/check_digest.py, which can be run against any produced digest JSON.

evals.prompt: Here's a paper PDF — give me a full digest. (attach an empirical ML paper PDF)
evals.expected_output: A Markdown report following the fixed section order AND a JSON digest saved to disk. All 10 schema sections non-empty; critique has both strengths and weaknesses; headline results cite Tables/Figures/Sections; code/arxiv/doi match the parser's meta.json.

assertions.text: Output JSON is valid and parseable
All 10 required sections are present and non-empty
critique contains both strengths and weaknesses
At least half of key_results cite a Table/Figure/Section/Eq
metadata.code_links is consistent with parser has_code_link (no invented code release)
doi / arxiv_id, if stated, match the parser-extracted values

evals.prompt: Is this paper any good? Should I read it in full? (attach a paper PDF with no code release)
evals.expected_output: A digest whose reproducibility section reports code_available=false and a risk rating with reasoning; the critique should weigh whether the contribution justifies a full read. No fabricated code link.
files: a paper .pdf without a code link

assertions.text: reproducibility.code_available is false when the parser finds no code link
reproducibility_risk is one of low/medium/high with a one-line rationale
critique gives a defensible read-it-or-not judgment grounded in the paper

evals.prompt: Digest this survey paper for my lit review. (attach a survey paper PDF)
evals.expected_output: paper_type is 'survey'; the digest applies the survey reading lens — judging taxonomy quality and synthesis vs enumeration rather than baselines/datasets.

assertions.text: critique evaluates taxonomy/synthesis quality (survey lens), not experimental baselines
